title: In the light look, the orange words and buttons are too faint to read easily
what: When the computer or phone is set to light mode, every ordinary orange button has orange words on a pale orange patch, about 3.5 to 1 against the background. Orange links and the solid orange buttons with white words reach about 4.3 to 1. Plain text needs at least 4.5 to 1. In bright light or with weaker eyesight the button words blur.
expected: Every word on every button and link reads at 4.5 to 1 or better in both the dark and the light look.
fix_line: Use a darker orange for words in the light look.

title: In the dark look, the red count on the menu is hard to read
what: The red bubble that counts what needs you is a light red with white numbers in the dark look, about 2.8 to 1. The numbers are small and bold, so they can be misread at a glance.
expected: The count reads at 4.5 to 1 or better.
fix_line: Use a deeper red behind the count, or dark numbers.

title: Many boxes have only a grey hint inside, no name, and the hint vanishes once you type
what: The why box for pausing a gym, the why box for signing a gym out everywhere, the note boxes on feedback and leads, the member box on a delete request, the gym-code box for deleting a gym for ever, the cancel reason, and the boxes for refusing or noting a payment have no name above them. The only words are a grey hint inside the box, which disappears as soon as you type, so you cannot check what the box was for. In the light look that grey hint is about 3.2 to 1, below the readable level.
expected: Every box has a name that stays visible above it, as the other forms in HQ already do.
fix_line: Wrap each of these boxes in the same named field the other forms use.

title: The gym list rows open a gym but do not show or say that they can be opened
what: Each gym row opens the gym when clicked or when Enter is pressed. A screen reader announces it only as a table row, not as something to open. The keyboard highlight is a background shade almost the same as the row, so you cannot see which gym is selected. Space does nothing. On a phone each gym is a plain card with no arrow, unlike the Needs you lines and the number tiles, which carry an arrow.
expected: Each gym is a real link with a clear highlight, and an arrow on the phone card.
fix_line: Make the gym name a link to the gym page, give rows a visible focus ring and an arrow on phones.

title: The Needs you page redraws itself every minute and loses your place
what: While the Needs you page is open, HQ rebuilds the whole page every minute unless you are typing in a box. If you have moved with the keyboard to a line, or a screen reader is reading the page, the selection jumps back to the top of the page and reading starts again.
expected: The page updates only the parts that changed and keeps the selected item where it was.
fix_line: Skip the redraw when nothing changed, and keep focus when it does.

title: A screen reader reads the read-log warning out again every minute
what: The red read-log warning on top of every page is rebuilt every minute as a fresh urgent message, so a screen reader breaks in and reads the same warning again each minute on every page.
expected: The warning is read once when it first appears or changes.
how_often: every minute while the warning shows
fix_line: Rebuild the warning only when its words change.

title: Moving to another page is silent for a screen reader, and the current page is shown by colour only
what: The current page in the side menu and bottom bar is marked only by colour. Nothing tells a screen reader which page is open. When you pick a page, the content changes, but the reading position does not move to the new heading and the tab title stays the same, so a screen reader user does not know the page changed.
expected: The current menu item is marked as current for screen readers. A new page moves the reading position to its heading.
fix_line: Mark the current menu item as current and move focus to the new page heading.

title: On a phone, the More sheet opens but the keyboard and screen reader stay on the page behind it
what: Tapping More slides up the menu sheet over a dark cover, but the selection stays on the More button. With a keyboard or screen reader you keep moving through the page hidden behind the cover before reaching the sheet. Escape and tapping the cover do close it.
expected: Opening More moves the selection into the sheet and keeps it there until the sheet closes.
how_often: every time More is opened with a keyboard or screen reader
fix_line: Move focus into the sheet when it opens and back to More when it closes.

title: Two things on the phone are small to tap: the back link on a gym page and Install app
what: On a phone, the All gyms back link on a gym page is only about one line of small text tall, about 22 pixels, because the rule that enlarges links skips it. The Install app button in the top bar is 36 pixels. Other buttons on the phone are 44 to 46 pixels.
expected: Every tappable thing on the phone is at least 44 pixels tall.
fix_line: Give the back link and Install app a 44 pixel tap height on phones.

title: HQ ignores the bigger text setting in the computer browser
what: All HQ text sizes are fixed. If the browser text size on a computer is set to large, HQ stays the same size. Zooming the page and the phone text size settings still work.
expected: HQ grows with the browser text size setting.
how_often: only for someone who set bigger text
fix_line: Size text relative to the browser setting instead of fixed pixels.

title: If you close the install pop-up, the Install app button disappears with no hint how to install later
what: Tapping Install app opens the browser install pop-up. If you close it, HQ hides the button and does not tell you that you can still install from the browser menu. The button may come back only on a later visit, if the browser offers it again.
expected: After the pop-up is closed, HQ keeps the button or a short line saying how to install from the browser menu.
how_often: once, after closing the install pop-up
fix_line: After a closed install pop-up, show a line saying to use the browser menu to install.

title: No automatic accessibility check ever runs on HQ
what: The automatic accessibility check in the build looks only at the gym admin app. HQ is never checked, so faint colours, missing names and keyboard traps on HQ are found only by hand.
expected: The same automatic check runs over every HQ page in the build.
fix_line: Add HQ pages to the cloud accessibility check.
